scopeBoundary.selectedBy: identity-and-evidence section 3 ("The effective registry is selected here, by name") and native-evidence section 11 both name native/capability-manifest-domains.v2.json
scopeBoundary.supersedes: delivery.v4.json capabilityManifestIdentity.valueDomains, within its own declared scope and nowhere else
scopeBoundary.codecSeparation: CVE1 is the CAPABILITY MANIFEST encoding and has nothing to do with the relation PAYLOAD codec. Relation payloads are canonical JSON C under foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json; the superseded relation payload CBOR profile and CVE1 are three different things and none substitutes for another.
scopeBoundary.platformDomainCaveat: Admitting a platformId here admits a capability manifest SCALAR under ADM-DOMAIN. It is not a platform admission, not a qualification lane, not a supported population and not a licence to run anywhere: platform admission is the security owner's (S8 platform_admit and the signed PlatformProfileSetV1) and a request naming an unselected platform is refused there, whatever a manifest declared. A provider declaring a capability for an unselected platform therefore obtains no product capability on it; nothing downstream reads this domain as a support claim.
scopeBoundary.inheritedVocabularyBroaderThanSelectedPr: This domain is the INHERITED delivery vocabulary, reproduced verbatim, and it is deliberately not narrowed here. The selected product promises exactly FOUR machine platform ids - linux-x86_64-gnu, linux-aarch64-gnu, macos-aarch64, macos-x86_64. The OWNING authority for that selection is the security unit's S8 platform table, which is the one machine platform vocabulary, together with native-capability-matrix.v2.json platformFamilies, which carries the identical four ids. S8 is also where Windows is excluded: it names Windows among the populations outside the selected support population, for which the core refuses rather than degrades. (The blind consumer-B v5 review cited admission-and-qualification section 5 item 1 for that exclusion; that citation is not where the selection lives. The review's own bytes remain the historical record and are not edited - this entry simply cites the actual owner.) windows-x86_64-msvc, windows-aarch64-msvc and linux-x86_64-musl are therefore members of this ENCODING domain and of no product promise.
scopeBoundary.everyReachableObjectTypeClassified: FOUR reachable object types, THREE records and ONE map, and the census is exhaustive over the four live manifests and the three synthetic vectors. The retained checker walks each admitted manifest and fails the run if it reaches an object that is in neither list.

ADM-TYPE.statement: Every scalar is admitted by EXACT JSON TYPE before its content is compared. schemaVersion is a JSON integer -- a boolean is not an integer, a float is not an integer, a numeric string is not a number -- and every other declared scalar is a JSON string. The type assertion is the gate; content comparison happens only after it passes.

ADM-CLOSED.statement: EVERY REACHABLE RECORD IS CLOSED, AND A MAP IS NOT A RECORD. Every JSON object reachable from a committed CapabilityManifestV1 -- the record itself, every element of every declared collection, every value of every declared map, and every object a later successor adds at any depth -- is either a RECORD or a MAP, and the schema says which by what it declares for it. A RECORD declares a KEY SET: it carries EXACTLY that key set, each key exactly once, with no undeclared member. A MAP declares a KEY DOMAIN: it carries no key set, closure does not apply to it, its keys are admitted by DL-DOM-1 against that domain, and its VALUES are governed by this property recursively -- so a map of records is closed at its records and A MAP WHOSE VALUES ARE SCALARS CLOSES NOTHING. A reachable object type that declares NEITHER a key set NOR a key domain is a schema defect and is inadmissible until it declares one; permissiveness is never the default.

ADM-DOMAIN.statement: EVERY SCALAR IN A COMMITTED CapabilityManifestV1 IS EITHER BOUND TO A NAMED REGISTRY OR DECLARED OPEN, AND THERE IS NO THIRD STATE. A bound scalar is admitted only if its value is a member of its registry, compared by EXACT NFC UTF-8 BYTES -- no case folding, no alias, no trimming, no prefix match, no normalisation of any kind. An OPEN position is one this schema declares open, with the declaration itself standing as the record that no registry constrains it. A position that is neither bound nor declared open is a schema defect, and it is inadmissible until it is one or the other.

ADM-ORDER.statement: DL-ORD-1. Every ordered collection in a COMMITTED CapabilityManifestV1 is already in its declared canonical order -- strictly ascending by the unsigned bytewise comparison of its declared sort key's NFC UTF-8 bytes. A committed manifest that is not is REJECTED, with domainReasonCode RELEASE.CAPABILITY_MANIFEST_NOT_CANONICAL. It is never sorted into shape by a consumer.

gateStatements.inheritedVerbatim: All four inherited gates are carried into the current entry point, not only the extended relation domain. ADM-TYPE is the exact JSON type assertion before any content comparison (a boolean is not an integer); ADM-CLOSED is the closed required key set; ADM-DOMAIN is the registry membership below; ADM-ORDER is strict ascending UNIQUE order in the declared traversal order, so a duplicate is an ordering violation and not merely an unsorted list.
